$notes: Human-authored, versioned rules table. A model never decides what to recommend, only how to word it. Every rule ships with static copy so the product works with no LLM.

Triggers: {metric, op, value} compares the raw metric value; {metric, category} compares the engine-derived z-category ('low' z<-1, 'typical', 'high' z>1) or an appearance category ('low'/'moderate'/'high', or a Norwood stage bucket). All triggers in a rule must fire (AND). min_confidence defaults to the metric's confidence_floor.

safety_tier: 1 self-directed, 2 OTC with irritation profile, 3 clinician territory (named, never dosed), 4 surgical/procedural (named, no links). Tier 3/4 never enter the ranked plan; they render in the 'To discuss with a professional' section.
cadence: 'daily' tasks define day completion; 'weekly' tasks have a target count per week; 'once' tasks are one-off setup. opens_week staggers tasks so week 1 is never overwhelming.
excludes: rule ids suppressed when this rule fires. always_on: fires regardless of findings when goal matches (foundational habits).
Copy must pass copy/voice.md: no comparative language, no 'mog', no 'subhuman', no degrading tiers, no dosing, no caloric figures.

rules.task_title: Hit your protein and movement targets for the day

copy.headline: Lower body fat gradually
copy.body: The line between jaw and neck is mostly soft tissue. Losing body fat slowly, about half a percent to one percent of bodyweight a week, with protein and resistance training, sharpens it more than anything done to the jaw.
copy.why_this: Your facial fat is high and your jaw-neck angle is wide. Both improve as body fat drops.

rules.task_title: Hit your protein and movement targets for the day

copy.headline: Lean out gradually
copy.body: Facial fat changes more than almost anything else about a face. Lose it slowly, about half a percent to one percent of bodyweight a week, and keep protein and lifting up so you hold on to muscle.
copy.why_this: Your facial fat is above the typical range.

rules.task_title: Resistance training session

copy.headline: Lift three times a week
copy.body: Lifting three times a week keeps your muscle while you lose fat. Without it, fat loss can leave a face looking gaunt.
copy.why_this: Fat loss looks sharper when you keep your muscle.

copy.headline: Jaw exercisers
copy.body: Placeholder entry so the exclusion graph has a target. Tier X: never emitted.

rules.task_title: Broad-spectrum SPF 30+ on face and neck

copy.headline: Daily broad-spectrum SPF
copy.body: Sun exposure causes most uneven skin over time. Put on broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher every morning, including cloudy days.
copy.why_this: Every skin goal depends on it.

rules.task_title: Gentle cleanse and moisturise, morning and night

copy.headline: A two-step routine, twice a day
copy.body: Use a gentle, fragrance-free cleanser and a plain moisturiser morning and night. Most unevenness comes from irritation and dryness, and these two clear much of it in a few weeks.
copy.why_this: Your skin evenness is below typical. Start with the basics and add actives once your skin has settled.

rules.task_title: Evening active (start 2 or 3 nights a week)

copy.headline: Add one over-the-counter active, slowly
copy.body: Pick one active for the evening: adapalene gel for texture and breakouts, or low-strength azelaic acid for redness and tone. Start two or three nights a week and build up. Some dryness or flaking early on is normal. Stop and see a pharmacist or dermatologist if irritation is more than mild.
copy.why_this: Your skin evenness is low. These have the best evidence of anything sold without a prescription.

rules.task_title: In bed by your target time

copy.headline: Protect your sleep
copy.body: Sleep-deprived faces are rated less healthy in controlled studies, mostly around the eyes. A consistent bedtime does more than any product.
copy.why_this: It's free and it shows quickly, around the eyes first.

rules.task_title: Drink water, and go easy on salt and alcohol tonight

copy.headline: Reduce morning puffiness
copy.body: Salt and alcohol in the evening and short sleep all show under your eyes the next morning. Drink water through the day, eat less salt late and keep a regular bedtime. Most eye creams are moisturiser.
copy.why_this: These are the easy changes for the eye area. Sleep does more.

rules.task_title: Tidy brows: remove strays between and below, keep the shape

copy.headline: Tidy your brows and keep their shape
copy.body: Remove the stray hairs between your brows and below the arch, and leave the shape alone. Thin brows make a face look older and more tired.
copy.why_this: It shows straight away and grows back if you don't like it.

rules.task_title: Book a haircut

copy.headline: Get a cut that works with your proportions
copy.body: A good haircut changes how your proportions look. With a long forehead, ask for volume at the sides and keep the top low. With a short forehead, add a little height on top. If your hairline is receding, keep it short there, because combing hair over it draws attention to it.
copy.why_this: It's quick and it grows out.

rules.task_title: Hair: no heat today, condition if you wash, style without pulling

copy.headline: Treat the hair you have gently
copy.body: This won't regrow hair, but it makes the hair you have look fuller. Use a gentle shampoo and conditioner, go easy on heat, and avoid tight styles that pull at your hairline.
copy.why_this: You picked hair as a goal. There's no risk, and it shows within weeks.

copy.headline: Hairline recession: treatments exist, and they work best early
copy.body: Your hairline is at a stage where recession is visible. Two treatments have strong evidence: topical minoxidil, sold over the counter, and oral finasteride, which is prescription-only and has side effects you should talk through with a doctor. A dermatologist or GP can advise in one appointment, and earlier is better. We don't recommend procedures or prescriptions and we have no financial relationship with any provider.
copy.why_this: Hairline stage estimated at Norwood 3 or above.

rules.task_title: Take a hairline reference photo in the same light

copy.headline: Keep an eye on the hairline
copy.body: A mature hairline is normal and isn't the same as recession. To tell them apart, take the same reference photo every few weeks. If the hairline moves, talk to a doctor about treatment early.
copy.why_this: Hairline estimated at Norwood 2, within normal adult variation.

rules.task_title: Retake your best photo from further back with 2× zoom

copy.headline: Shoot from further back
copy.body: At arm's length a phone makes your nose look about thirty percent wider and shrinks your ears and jaw. Step back a metre or more and zoom in, or have someone else take the photo.
copy.why_this: Measured in a 2018 JAMA study.

rules.task_title: Find your window: soft light from slightly above and to one side

copy.headline: Use soft, slightly directional light
copy.body: Flat light from the front hides the structure of a face, and hard light from overhead exaggerates it. Use window light from slightly above and to one side, and face it.
copy.why_this: After distance, light changes how your face photographs more than anything else.

rules.task_title: Posture check: ears over shoulders, chin level

copy.headline: Bring your head back over your shoulders
copy.body: Holding your head forward softens the line between jaw and neck. Bring your ears back over your shoulders and keep your chin level. Your bone structure stays the same, but the line looks sharper straight away.
copy.why_this: It's free and works straight away. If your jaw-neck angle is wide, part of that is posture.

rules.task_title: Shape the beard: keep length along the jaw, fade the cheeks and neck

copy.headline: Shape your beard to widen the jaw
copy.body: Facial hair can widen and square the lower face. Keep density and a little length along the jaw and chin, fade the cheeks, and set the neckline a finger above the Adam's apple.
copy.why_this: Your jaw is narrower than typical next to your cheekbones, and a beard adds width there.

rules.task_title: Try growing stubble along the jaw for two weeks

copy.headline: Consider stubble along the jaw
copy.body: Stubble along the jaw and chin adds visual width where your face is narrowest. Give it two weeks to see whether it suits you.
copy.why_this: Your jaw is narrow next to your cheekbones, and you are clean-shaven.

copy.headline: About mewing
copy.body: Tongue-posture routines are promoted for a profile like yours. The British Orthodontic Society and the American Association of Orthodontists both said in 2025 there is no scientific evidence they change adult facial shape. Good head posture is still worth having, but it won't move bone.
copy.why_this: Your profile convexity is outside the typical range, which is the finding these routines are marketed to.

copy.headline: Profile convexity: an orthodontist can tell you what it is
copy.body: Your profile is markedly convex. That can come from jaw position, teeth or soft tissue, and only a clinical assessment can tell which. An orthodontic consultation is often free or inexpensive. We don't recommend procedures or prescriptions and we have no financial relationship with any provider.
copy.why_this: Soft-tissue facial convexity measured well below the typical range.

copy.headline: Chin projection
copy.body: Your chin sits well behind the nose-to-chin reference line. A board-certified facial plastic or maxillofacial surgeon could assess it. Posture and facial hair change how it looks without changing the chin itself. We don't recommend procedures or prescriptions and we have no financial relationship with any provider.
copy.why_this: Soft-tissue chin measured more than 6 mm behind the E-line.

copy.headline: Nose-lip angle: a camera note
copy.body: Your nose-lip angle is sharper than typical. That comes from structure and won't change, but it photographs better with the camera at or slightly above eye level.
copy.why_this: Nasolabial angle below the typical range.

copy.headline: Nose width and camera distance
copy.body: Your nose base is wide next to your eye spacing. Close-up phone photos exaggerate this most, by about thirty percent at arm's length, so photos from further back will look different from selfies. Your scan was taken at a controlled distance.
copy.why_this: Nasal base width above the typical range.

rules.task_title: Find your better side in soft, even light

copy.headline: Every face is asymmetric, and light changes how much it shows
copy.body: Every face is asymmetric, and uneven light exaggerates it. Even light from the front shows it least. Most people have a side that photographs better, so find yours.
copy.why_this: Your symmetry is a little below typical. The lighting check passed, so the capture didn't cause it.

rules.task_title: Lip balm with SPF

copy.headline: Look after your lips
copy.body: Chapped lips look unhealthy and are the easiest thing on this list to fix. Put on a plain balm with SPF when you do your sunscreen.
copy.why_this: A small addition to the skin routine.

rules.task_title: Water with every meal

copy.headline: Drink water with meals
copy.body: The evidence that hydration changes skin is weaker than the internet says. Mild dehydration does show in the face by evening, and ruling it out costs nothing.
copy.why_this: It backs up the other habits.

rules.task_title: No alcohol tonight

copy.headline: Cut back on alcohol
copy.body: Alcohol adds calories, disrupts sleep and causes puffiness the next day. Cutting the number of days you drink is easier to stick to than quitting.
copy.why_this: Your facial fat is high, and alcohol often adds to it without people noticing.

copy.headline: Prescription retinoids: worth asking about
copy.body: Your skin evenness is well below typical. The best-evidenced treatment for texture and tone is prescription tretinoin, and persistent breakouts have prescription options too. A dermatologist or GP, often by telehealth, can prescribe. We don't recommend procedures or prescriptions and we have no financial relationship with any provider.
copy.why_this: Skin evenness index below 0.50.

rules.task_title: Reference photo: same spot, same light, same distance

copy.headline: One reference photo a week
copy.body: Take a plain photo in the same spot, light and distance each week. It stays in your camera roll and the app never reads it.
copy.why_this: It shows change over the eight weeks without scanning every day.
